initial_prompt: Hot take: most "self-care" advice is just consumerism dressed up as wellness. Buy this journal, take this bath, use this app. When did taking care of yourself become another thing to optimize and monetize?

messages.content: Hot take: most "self-care" advice is just consumerism dressed up as wellness. Buy this journal, take this bath, use this app. When did taking care of yourself become another thing to optimize and monetize?

You're onto something real. There's definitely a commercial machinery that's turned "self-care" into a product category rather than just... living sensibly.

The weirdest part is how it inverted the original meaning. "Self-care" came from activism and healthcare contexts - Audre Lorde writing about preservation as a political act for people doing exhausting justice work, or medical professionals talking about patients managing chronic conditions. It meant: you can't pour from an empty cup, rest is resistance, basic needs matter.

Then it got aesthetic-ified. Now it's often signaling class and leisure - who has time for the 45-minute morning routine with the special tea and the gratitude journal and the curated playlist?

But I think there's a messier reality underneath the hot take too:

Some people genuinely *don't know* how to rest or what feels good to them - they've been optimizing and producing for so long they've lost the thread. A bath bomb or a journal prompt might be training wheels back to "oh right, I'm allowed to feel okay." Clumsy, commodified training wheels, but still.

And sometimes the consumerist version is just... easier to talk about than the real thing. "I need better sleep hygiene and this pillow spray" is more socially acceptable than "I'm so fried I can barely function and my life needs structural changes I don't know how to make."

The darker read: turning it into products keeps it individual. Buy your way to wellness, don't ask about 60-hour work weeks or healthcare costs or why everyone's so fucking tired.

What does actual self-care look like to you, stripped of the Instagram aesthetics?
